recommendation: Keep the fix. It preserves the FHIR-8502 MedicationAdministration application and prevents stale MedicationOrder/MedicationDispense rate guidance from misleading R6 implementers. If the broader FHIR-51540 DosageDetails design is later substantially reworked, re-check this wording with that change family.
issue_request: FHIR-8502 was a Published Pharmacy issue resolved Persuasive with Modification. It asked to fix a contradictory MedicationAdministration.dosage.rate[x] comment, change the MedicationOrder dosage rate guidance to use a new or updated order/request for rate changes, and remove the corresponding rate comment from MedicationDispense.
initial_application: Git commit 0c6541df60 explicitly applied #8502 by changing MedicationOrder and MedicationAdministration rate comments and removing the MedicationDispense rate comment. Current MedicationAdministration.dosage.rate[x] still says rate changes captured during administration should be separate MedicationAdministration events with specific rates and times. The later FHIR-12840 refactor moved DosageInstruction wording into the reusable Dosage datatype, carrying forward the old request-specific rate guidance.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini keeps Dosage and the MedicationAdministration, MedicationDispense, and MedicationRequest resources in build scope. Later R6 dosage work introduced DosageDetails, changing MedicationRequest, MedicationDispense, and MedicationStatement dosageInstruction from repeated Dosage elements to one DosageDetails element with steps/components for complex regimes. Current dosage narrative and resource introduction pages already describe that model, so the old generic new-MedicationRequest wording and MedicationDispense multiple-dosageInstruction wording were stale.
reconciliation: Updated source/datatypes/dosage.xml so Dosage.doseAndRate.rate[x] tells implementers to use the dosage structure available in the containing context, such as DosageDetails steps, or a new/updated MedicationRequest when the request itself changes. Updated MedicationDispense.dosageInstruction to point to DosageDetails rather than impossible repeated dosageInstruction instances, and removed the copied dosageInstruction rate-change comment from MedicationDispense.doseAdministrationAid.
source_changes: source/datatypes/dosage.xml: generalized Dosage.doseAndRate.rate[x] rate-change guidance to the containing dosage context and DosageDetails steps, retaining new/updated MedicationRequest only when the request changes.

source/medicationdispense/structuredefinition-MedicationDispense.xml: changed dosageInstruction guidance from repeated dosageInstruction instances to DosageDetails, and removed the copied dosageInstruction comment from doseAdministrationAid.

related_jiras.note: Renamed DosageInstruction to Dosage and explains how the MedicationOrder rate comment became reusable Dosage source.
Current source implements DosageDetails for complex dosage regimes; this makes the literal new-MedicationRequest guidance stale, but this run does not decide FHIR-51540.
Applied follow-up removed DosageDetails.simple and confirms current complex dosage representation uses steps/components.
Older MedicationPrescription comment introduced multiple-dosageInstruction wording; current R6 DosageDetails makes that wording stale for MedicationDispense.

Introduced doseAdministrationAid and appears to have copied the stale dosageInstruction comment onto that packaging element; this commit removes only that copied comment and does not audit FHIR-52892.
